name: Mathurā
aka: Mathura, Mathurā-maṇḍala, Madhupurī, Viśrāma-ghāṭa, Vishram ghat
about:
The twelve famous forests of Mathurā-maṇḍala — on the east bank of the Yamunā: (1) Bhadravana, (2) Bhāṇḍīravana, (3) Lauhavana, (4) Bilvavana and (5) Mahāvana; on the west bank: (6) Tālavana, (7) Madhuvana, (8) Kumudavana, (9) Bahulāvana, (10) Kāmyavana, (11) Khadiravana and (12) Śrī Vṛndāvana.
The twenty-four ghāṭs of Mathurā — south of Viśrāma-ghāṭa: Avimukta, Adhirūḍha, Guhya, Prayāga, Kanakhala, Tinduka, Sūrya, Vaṭasvāmī, Dhruva, Ṛṣi, Mokṣa and Koṭi-tīrtha; north of it: Maṇikarṇikā, Asikuṇḍa, Saṁyamana, Dhārāpatana, Nāga, Vaikuṇṭha, Ghaṇṭābharaṇa, the Go-ghāṭa, Kṛṣṇagaṅgā, Cakra-tīrtha (the confluence with the Sarasvatī), Daśāśvamedha and Vighnarāja.
Dhruva-ghāṭa is where Dhruva performed austerities (bathing and tarpaṇa are recommended in the pitṛ-pakṣa); the goddess Mahāvidyā, with the Mahāvidyā-kuṇḍa, is within Mathurā-kṣetra; Dhyāna-kuṇḍa, where Kṛṣṇa meditated on Śrī Rādhā.

name: Madhuvana
location: Two and a half miles south-west of Mathurā; the present village is called Mahalī
about: One of the twelve forests of Vraja. East of the village is Dhruva-ṭilā, the place of Dhruva's austerities; south-west of it is Madhu-kuṇḍa. Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma grazed the cows here, and here Balarāma became intoxicated by drinking madhu.

name: Mahāvana
aka: Mahavana, Mahaban, Gokula, Gokul, Purāṇa Gokula
location: In Vraja-maṇḍala, on the east bank of the Yamunā
about: The great forest: the place of the childhood pastimes of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. To see: Nanda Mahārāja's danta-dhāvana-ṭilā and below it the gopīs' havelī; the places where Pūtanā was liberated, the cart was broken and Tṛṇāvarta was killed; in Nanda's house the dadhi-mahala; the place of Kṛṣṇa's ṣaṣṭhī-pūjā; Āśikhāmbā; the temple of Śyāmalālā; Kṛṣṇa's mortar (udūkhala); the Nanda-kūpa; the cowsheds of the king of Vraja.

name: Nandagrāma
about: Nandīśvara: the Nandagrāma of Mathurā-maṇḍala. Jāvaṭa, the home of Abhimanyu, is two miles to its north-east.

name: Jāvaṭa
about: The house of Abhimanyu (Bhakti-ratnākara 5.1069). West of the village is the Rādhākānta temple; east, the Kiśorī temple and the Kiśorī-kuṇḍa. At the nearby Vatsakhora Śrī Rādhā, dressed as Subala, met Kṛṣṇa; in a forest of beri (kula) trees Kṛṣṇa gave his signal by calling like a cuckoo.

name: Varṣāṇā
about:
Vṛṣabhānupura is another name of Varṣāṇā, the village of Śrī Rādhā. Near Śrī Rādhā's temple is Dāna-gaḍa; Māna-gaḍa (Māna-parvata), the place of the māna-līlā, is in Varṣāṇā. On a hill north-west of Gahvaravana is Mayūra-kuṭī, with a seat (baiṭhaka) of Vallabhācārya.
Around it: Muktā-kuṇḍa, where Rādhā and the gopīs planted a field of pearls; Mohinī-kuṇḍa to the south; Piri-pukur to the north, where Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa met on the pretext of gathering pīlu fruits; Bhānu-khora to the east, the kuṇḍa of King Vṛṣabhānu; Dohanī-kuṇḍa nearby, where the cows were milked; Pīyāso village to the north-east; Uccagāṁva to the north-west, with Dehi-kuṇḍa and Śrī Rādhā's footprints on its ghāṭ; and, at Vihāra-kuṇḍa, the birthplace of the sakhī Citrā.

name: Kāmyavana
location: In Mathurā-maṇḍala, one of the twelve forests
about: Many places to see: Śrī Vṛndā-devī, Śrī Kāmeśvara Śiva, the Vimalā-kuṇḍa, the Setubandha, Kṛṣṇa's footprints, the cave of Vyomāsura, the Bhojanasthalī and the «eighty-four pillars». On the bank of the Vimalā-kuṇḍa is the samādhi of the siddha Jayakṛṣṇa dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja. Also Madhusūdana-kuṇḍa, and the Vedakuṇḍa lake (Bhakti-ratnākara 5.877).
